prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale ground excludes spacecraft/launch/external processing; delivers predictable-latency, quality-documented imagery. Mission Control Center (Bluebell: local-voice-only) owns authorization/readiness/schedules/routing. Flight Dynamics Facility (Mistral: legacy-shift-logs) supplies orbit/maneuver/navigation/visibility/pointing. Mission Planning System converts approved demands/constraints/bookings into plans; planning/release segregated; Command Validation Gateway must validate uplinks. Telemetry Ingest Service receives spacecraft frames/contact-status/flow-indicators, validates framing/time-continuity, records reception metadata, distinguishes interruptions, supplies operations/engineering/processing; produces Pass Replay Packet for post-contact engineering reconstruction. Orbit Determination Engine consumes tracking, produces controlled orbit knowledge/Doppler Residual Report; supports state-updates/visibility/maneuver-constraints/pointing. Payload Processing Facility (Forgehouse: consoles/shift-logs) coordinates processing/calibration/quality/distribution. Primary Processing Cluster nominal; Backup Processing Cluster controlled-failover/lower-preference, firewall/return-paths routinely tested. Transfers to Long Term Archive contact-rate-limited protecting telemetry/control-monitoring; archive preserves data/products/evidence. Product Quality Service checks dissemination; User Services Portal provides search/orders/status/support. Network Control System (Lantern) owns circuits/routing/allocations/readiness/contact-records; sends antenna-status/link-configuration/timing-references/routing-readiness to Mission Control Center before passes. Ground Network Manager (Juniper: standing-rosters) owns antenna/link availability, readiness/conflicts/maintenance/staffing/site-coordination; issues Antenna Deicing Notice; pins critical-paths before acquisition. Spacecraft Operations Team owns safety/contact-decisions; monitors mode/power/thermal/attitude/command-counters/storage/faults; displays emphasize deviations. Console lead declares pass-status, authorizes validated commands, pauses unexpected configurations; telemetry engineer checks quality/loss/latency/continuity/command-confidence; spacecraft systems engineer checks flight-rules/health, records anomalies. Flight Dynamics Team uses tracking/validated-time-tags, separates clock-bias/tracking-error. Payload Calibration Team owns performance/quality. Cybersecurity Desk monitors/escalates, sends Security Exception Ticket; blocking coordinated with manager protects contacts/recovery. Shift security reviews/correlations required. North S-Band Antenna/South S-Band Antenna interchangeable command/low-rate-telemetry; Kiruna X-Band Antenna/Svalbard X-Band Antenna

New part:
S093: The Mission Control Center coordinates with the Payload Processing Facility when instrument mode changes, data downlink priorities, or reception gaps could affect downstream processing.
S094: The Payload Calibration Team sends the Calibration Patch Bundle after calibration analysis identifies an approved update for payload processing behavior.
S095: Subsystem specialists are not expected to staff every live contact, but they must be reachable during planned critical activities and whenever a console operator declares an off-nominal condition.
S096: Escalation from the Mission Control Center begins with the console lead, moves to the responsible discipline lead, and then reaches mission management when the condition threatens spacecraft safety, contact continuity, or recovery schedule.
S097: The Spacecraft Operations Team and Flight Dynamics Team coordinate closely before orbit-control activities so that command timing, attitude constraints, tracking expectations, and post-burn assessment steps remain consistent.
S098: When telemetry indicates a possible onboard fault, operators preserve the command state, avoid discretionary commanding, and request specialist review before changing spacecraft configuration.
S099: The Mission Planning System receives operational constraints from mission control after anomalies, station outages, or spacecraft configuration changes require adjustment of future contacts or payload activities.
S100: At the end of each shift, the Mission Control Center records unresolved actions, open engineering questions, and expected specialist responses so that the next operations crew can maintain continuity without relying on informal handover.
S101: Mission planning begins when observation requests arrive through the User Services Portal or from internal operations channels at the Mission Control Center.
S102: The Mission Planning System, also called Cedar in this section, is the authoritative tool for assembling candidate observation timelines and associated ground contact activities.
S103: Each request is checked for requester authority, target definition, time sensitivity, acquisition mode, expected data volume, and any handling restrictions before it is admitted to the planning pool.
S104: The User Services Portal records the request state so that external users can distinguish accepted requests from those still awaiting technical review.
S105: The Spacecraft Operations Team reviews late operational requests when they affect spacecraft attitude, thermal margin, stored command capacity, or contact preparation.
S106: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit predictions and visibility assumptions that the planning cycle uses to determine feasible imaging windows and ground contacts.
S107: The Mission Planning System combines request priority, instrument availability, contact opportunities, onboard storage margin, and downlink capacity into a draft activity schedule.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
